chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him), Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Rizq Allah ibn al-Ala, from Sulayman ibn Amr al-Sarraj, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The clay of the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) is taken from near the grave to the extent of seventy ba's.

key_terms.بَاعاً: ba', a unit of measurement (approx. 4-5 meters)

ai.seo_question: What is the permissible distance for collecting clay from the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the permissibility of collecting blessed clay (turab) from the vicinity of Imam Husayn’s grave, defining the sacred zone as seventy ba's. This ruling underscores the Shia practice of seeking spiritual barakah through physical connection to the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the sanctity of the grave site to the broader theological concept of the Imam as a locus of divine presence.
